question.text: Skyvault Ventures (Cat I AIF — Angel Fund) is investing INR 15 crore in a DPIIT-recognised startup at a subscription price higher than the independent valuer's DCF fair value. Historically, this triggered 'Angel Tax' concerns. What is the position under the Finance Act 2024 with effect from 1 April 2025?

answer.text: Angel tax (Section 56(2)(viib)) has been ABOLISHED with effect from 1 April 2025, eliminating this tax risk for the investee company.
Angel tax continues to apply at a 30% rate at investor level.
Angel tax only applies to non-resident investors now.
Angel tax has been increased to 40% from FA 2024.

explanation.text: The Logic: The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 repealed Section 56(2)(viib) — the so-called "angel tax" provision — with effect from assessment year 2025-26 (transactions on or after April 1, 2025). Previously, if a closely-held company issued shares at a premium exceeding the prescribed fair market value, the excess was taxable in the company's hands as "income from other sources." Repeal eliminates this investee-company-level tax risk for above-FMV subscriptions by Angel Funds and VC funds. The Trap: Option B retains the now-abolished regime; Option C invents a non-resident-only version; Option D claims a rate hike that did not occur — the provision was scrapped entirely. Note: The XIX-D workbook chapter cited covers capital gains and Finance Act 2025 capital-gain rates but does not specifically describe the Section 56(2)(viib) angel-tax repeal or its effective date. The repeal should be confirmed from the Income-tax Act and the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 directly. Pre-April-2025 transactions may still be under litigation under the old regime; GAAR remains an overlay concern.
